Author: @living_paladin_esterias2048
Content: my Partner and I are on the fence about a Bloodborne Remake. While I enjoyed the Demons Souls remake quite a bit, Fromsoft uses its environmental lighting to set the foundation for its atmospheres. i found the environments in this lost a HUGE chunk of their identity when they were brought forward into this higher fidelity. Playing early fromsoft titles is like playing a fairy tale, the colour balance is adjusted depending on the feeling whatever environment you're in is trying to cultivate in you, its what makes Blight town so grime-y when you're in there and unassuming when you're looking down at it from above. Bloodborne is the same for me, the haziness of Yharnam makes the world feel somewhere between a dream and reality. if Yharnam isn't simultaneously wet, steamy, and steeped in hazy incense then i truly don't want to see it remade. Maybe i'm just being difficult, but i truly believe every element, every sun beam, is placed with careful intention to make every corner of FROMSOFTs titles so screenshot-able. Sure it gets janky in some spots, but i'm sorry if any element of the visual story telling is lost like it was in the Demons Souls remake then i do not want Blue Point or anyone else to come near BB. i'll take a Re-release with higher FPS before i take a remake

Content: I apologize if someone else already said this, but as someone who practices historical martial arts and fights with sword on a weekly basis, 35:30 the reason that's considered a Bastard sword is because in order to hold it properly in 2 hands you have to hold the pommel. Put simply you loose a lot of control of the weapon butting your hands together like a baseball bat like you did. to hold it properly your hands would be about a hands width apart, bastard swords can achieve that by holding onto the pommel, true longsword grips are design with that space in mind so you don't usually need to hold the pommel for them. the biggest distinction between the types of sword is the blade length Bastard swords are short and light enough for single handed use, Longswords are exclusively 2 handed. lovely weapon, sorry for gushing on something you clearly already know lol us sword freaks are very passionate

Content: A laurel is a crown made of (traditionally) laurel tree branches. It was presented as a symbol of victory at sporting events (the original Olympics) in Ancient Greece and Rome. Author: @GilraenTook
Content:
IV and VI are my favourite Final Fantasies.  I /hate/ VII.  VI does have a good bit of steampunk, but it isn't modern technology like cars.  The pixel remakes are available for PC and Switch, even if that does mean you've got to deal with the re-translated opera in FFVI.  It is a bit silly and serious like you mentioned.  

Have you played any of the Elder Scrolls games?  American RPGs (alms for the poor.  Pls help me escape this hellhole...  I just wanna be a cheesemaker with a little farm in a civilised country...) but they're pretty cool.  I've put probably thousands of hours into Daggerfall and Morrowind, and I think at least Daggerfall is free on GoG.  Not sure if the later games are good because they seemed to my autistic brain to be trendy and it sort of spoiled me for them before I ever tried them-once I had a computer I could play them on anyway.  I'll play them eventually, just not now.  The first two Baldur's Gate games are also ARPGs that are fantastic.  Definitely medieval feels to them, and they're really fun.  Hm.  My best friend loves the Pathfinder games, though the world-building is a bit much for my taste.  I have gotten lost in them **looks sheepish**  Any of the other D&D games like Neverwinter Nights or Icewind Dale, especially the ones that have enhanced editions, are always good (with the exception of me not liking Planescape: Torment that much,  though it DOES have a lot of humour, even if it is a darker tone).  Some of the Wizardry and Ultima games have that style to them, though some of the older games (sort of like the old NES games) could be brutal with needing to do things like making your own maps, or figuring out where to go with next to no guidance.  

Eh, oops, you asked for more JRPGs, didn't you?

Author: @connorrekdahl3754
Content: The Lord of the Rings books are so good. I read the hobbit and the 3 main books and it took me almost all last year, with other book in-between, and for how much I love the movies I have to say that the books are so much better. Especially the second book/movie. Even tho the movies are about 11 hours, the books make it seem like the briefest summary of the main events and even to the point of skipping whole chapters with one single scene. Take farmer magot’s part, pretty much non-existent in the movie. Also Tom Bombadill’s part which was one of the best in the first book… I would also say that the movies are far more “dry” than the books. The books describe the settings in such a way that movies could never do, it brings life even to the most dead parts. The style of writing is somewhat difficult but once you get it down it’s all the more beautiful. I will say, though, that the movies have some more punch and impactful moments, certain speeches, like Sam’s speech in Oshiliath in a battle that Frodo and Sam were never a part of in the book. That was one of the best moments in movie history but it was not a part of the official literature. So in some regards the movies do better than the books.

Author: @calebdemeter2809
Content:
Here's my take on LOTR, take it or leave it. The movies are not better than the books like Sean said, but they are absolutely more accessible. They deliver the essence of Tolkeins masterpiece in a form that is much easier to engage with for at least a dozen reasons. While the movies are stunningly good adaptations, they not only remove material (which was necessary for the constraints ot film) but also miss the entire point of several mey characters and themes. So as an artwork and an example of storytelling the books are clearly superior, but if someone has difficulty engaging with them for any reason, whether it be personal taste, busy schedule, the older vocabulary, or any other reason, then the movies are a Godsend to be able to experience Tolkein's amazing story. And from the point of view of that person, I totally understand thinking that the movies are better, because for that person they are better. They solve the problems that made that person dislike the books.

Tldr; the books are better, but the movies are vastly more accessible and thats a fantastic thing.

P.S. I also struggle to commit to reading through books that long, but the Audible version of LOTR is fantastic and I listen to it often

Content: I’m going to have to strongly disagree with your 10/10 remake statement. They made so many artistic changes that absolutely breaks the lore in this game. If you don’t care about lore at all, then yeah maybe it is a great remake. But it shatters so much lore. The character designs make absolutely no sense at times, Boletaria is supposed to be lived in, but it’s rundown in the remake. The Fools idol is meant to lure in people with hope, but it doesn’t give off that vibe whatsoever in the remake. Just too many changes made for me to probably ever play this remake again. Again if you absolutely do not care about the lore, then yeah the remake is fine. But as someone who is really attached to the Souls lore, the remake is maybe a 6/10. And that’s only because it looks pretty and plays well. Needless to say I absolutely do not Trust Blue Point to make a faithful adaptation of Bloodborne. If it isn’t FromSoft remaking it then I don’t want it.

Author: @jeffreymeent9839
Content:
since sean gave his ranking of the games at the end, i feel inclined to share mine as well. no one cares i know, i just think it's fun for everyone to share their different rankings and to talk about why you have these preferences, so please respond with your own ranking and open up conversation about it, my autistic enthusiasm will be made very happy! 

also side note, i myself have never actually played through any of these games cause i suck ass at them, i've been stuck on ds1 for about 3 or 4 years, so since i bought the whole trilogy ambitiously, in between the road after taurus demon to the bell gargoyles, so basically the start of the game, that's how much i suck. luckily youtube exists so i can watch competent people play them for me so i can enjoy one of my special interests regardless!

so my ranking:
1. bloodborne
2. dark souls
3. dark souls 3
4. elden ring
5. demon's souls
6. dark souls 2
7. sekiro

sekiro is the only one that i haven't delved into all that much, it just never grasped my interest as much as all the other ones did, but perhaps seeing sean's playthrough when that time comes it ends up higher on the list. i don't know much about the game as of now and from what i have seen from it my prejudice places it in last place. but alas, in all fairness it's also the only one that i don't really know anything about except for having seen the gameplay a few times. the only other ones i am/was rusty on are ds2 & demon's souls, but i know still a bit of the lore, many of the bosses, a good idea of what the gameplay style looks like/feels like to control (for the competent people that ain't me lmao), so i can place them fairly without any doubt. now having just watched this whole video i have a much clearer view on demon's souls again ofc, but it already edged slightly over ds2 in my ranking before that so the only change there is that now demon's souls edges out ds2 a bit more than slightly solely because of understanding the whole game much better while ds2 is still very rusty in remembrance. 

the top 4 are very clearly and very distinctly ranked for me tho, and i love them all to bits for each their respective reasons. but to me they're also each placed above the other with certainty, no close edges there. as for sekiro, one day my judgement on the game could be subject to change drastically, but i'm like 99% sure that it'll never come close for me to that top 4, the highest it can reach is 5th place, which even that i doubt it'll ever top demon's souls for me, and i see it unlikely that sekiro will edge over ds2 either. so that's why i feel like adding sekiro to my ranking despite not knowing the game well at all comparatively is a viable choice nonetheless, i trust my judgement. 

anyway, i might've overexplained a few bits here and there, blame it on my autistic adhd enthusiasm stimulated by caffeine & insomnia. to be fair tho, this is my version of keeping it global & general, i could write 20 more paragraphs if i'd enter any details. 
but now it's your turn to share your rankings, and add as much explanations as you like, i enjoy reading whole paragraphs full of all your arguments & reasons just as much, even preferable, as simply just the 7 numbers with the 7 names underneath one another. whatever floats your boat!

Author: @greenxlady4585
Content:
After discovering this channel in very early 2017 and watching it four more than four years (after which the hyperfixation faded and I decided to take a break), I'm glad I came back half a year ago, just in time to see the Fromsoft playthroughs while they're still fairly fresh. All I knew about Fromsoft before Jack was "Git Gud" and the Dark Souls Take on Me video, and I never really had an interest in them before as watching horror games makes my anxiety skyrocket, but he talked about them so much and so often that I ended up cracking and watching his Bloodborne series from 2022. This was one of the best decisions I ever made! I'd never be able to play these games myself, but the combination of the games' aesthetics along with the sound design and stories made me fall in love with them. But I wouldn't nearly like them that much if it wasn't for Seán. Hearing him gush about the things he liked, pointing out small details that I probably wouldn't have noticed, and telling us the story in his unique way along with fleshing out the characters of both Dinklebamp and BONK while plowing through the game with a level of skill that I could never reach myself, but mostly him using the less tense moments to tell us about his experiences, his interests, the way he views the world, all of these make these videos some of my favourites on the channel. 
I hope that others who don't know Fromsoft will give these videos a try and gain a new appreciation for them, just like I have. Even if the games themselves aren't your cup of tea, simply seeing Seán smile with pure joy and giddiness at getting to play some of his favourite games here and tell people about what he loves is reason enough to watch them.
Thank you, Seán, for sharing this joy with us, and although all I know about Sekiro is "Parry time" and "Big White Snake", I can't wait for that video so I can see why exactly it's so high on your ranking. Godspeed!

P.S.: When you wondered about the expression "Resting on one's laurels": Laurel wreaths come from the laurel tree and were awarded to both the victors of big sporting events, specifically the Pythian games at Delphi held in honour of Apollo to whom the laurel tree was sacred, and later to martial victors in Roman times. That's where the expression comes from, it means to rely on past glory and achievements to maintain one's status without striving for new ones. But you may have also come in contact with laurels while cooking, where you may have heard its other name of "bay laurel", or simply bay leaves. They are a fairly common ingredient in different kinds of stew or sauce, although I think they're a bit too tough to be edible themselves. I don't blame people for not making the connection, I've only ever heard the name "laurel leaves" used in German or French, but not English.

Author: @geckosnest6297
Content:
Tips for Each Area in the Order that I Play:

1-1: If you get the dragon to start breathing fire on the bridge, you can go to where the blue dragon is and pick up those items
1-2: The Tower Knight can be cheesed by using the bow you find in the area, along with buying some arrows.
2-1: Don't have anything here, it's an ez area
3-1: Fool's Idol can be found out by locking on. if there is a health bar over them, it is a fake.
4-1: If you have enough stam and use a shield, the rolling skellies don't stagger you as much. Also, the yellow hawk takes more damage than the body.
2-2: Best Place to Farm Anything (On Black World Tendency). The crystal lizards don't run away if you use a bow and use thief ring
2-3: Use a Greatshield to smash the obstacles.
3-2: After you cut the heart down, you can find a Ring of Avarice where it falls.
3-3: Fun place to roleplay as a boss. Especially if you just don't heal.
4-2: Best Place to Farm Souls. Also, you can use Thief Ring and Poison Mist to cheese Old Hero if you weak.
4-3: BEST MUSIC.
5-1: Take it slow and bring fire for the boss. 
5-2: Fight the big guys on land, not in the swamp. Also, you can skip the village area by just going around it through the swamp and climbing onto the platform.
5-3: Garl Vinland is especially weak to parrying. Also, don't go into the swamp part unless you want to get ganked by babies.
1-3: Use the Fat Officials outfit to get best waifu. Also, Biorr destroys Penetrator.
1-4: Use Thief Ring and Poison Fog to cheese the Final Boss. If you hide to the side of the stairs and wait for him to walk over... he will turn around.

TL;DR: Use Lava Bow/Magic and shields to destroy this game.

Author: @Bestboy_Rhys
Content:
So this is random and confusing to anyone who hasn't gotten to the end of the video yet but I wanted to bring this up in case Sean sees this and gives his input. 

I wasn't all that big on Evangelion, to be honest. Part of it was me going into it thinking okay this is a mecha anime there's going to be some insane battle scenes that blow my mind but really we don't actually get much in the way of mech fights in the anime, it mostly focuses on the cosmic scale of everything going on in the background. 

My biggest issue with Evangelion is the ending. And this happens a lot with anime who lost funding or have to wrap up quickly due to release dates, quotas and obligation, but the ending felt like a complete 180 from the rest of the show. I also didn't like that they had to reboot it so many times. The End of Evangelion movie kind of sceeved me out in a lot of ways too. I've been unable to really get into the reboots because every time I start them I just get turned off because of how the original went. 

That's not to say it's not a good anime, or that people who enjoy it are invalid. I just didn't enjoy it the way most fans of the series did I guess.

Author: @Highyeena
Content:
I may not 100% understand what you are getting at with ff9, but I *think* i understand what you're after on some level -- though the 3 games i can think of aren't *exactly* the same, they scratch a sort of "slightly whimsical" or "slightly out of place" feeling -- Lies of P is a soulslike that sort of takes itself seriously, but acknowledges that the source material is a book most people consider sort of "whimsical" and leans into that, too. Most of the npcs are basically caricatures because of it -- but not super serious or 100% kooky. Valheim and Enshrouded are both survival crafting games and have a very particular feel about them -- Enshrouded being fantasy oriented and Valheim being Norse oriented but with fantasy added in later on! I'm not personally a big fan of survival crafting games, but Valheim and Enshrouded are a cut above.

Honorary mentions to Dragon Age: Origins (game still goes hard as heck), Okami (more "feudal japan" but with that same sort of "Serious-but-not" story and characters), and Children of Mana (and the other Mana games -- Children is just my personal favorite)

Author: @theradioactiveplayer3461
Content:
The medieval period is generally held to start with the fall* of the Western Roman empire (476 CE), and end sometime in the 1400s (though an argument can be made that its end began in 1349, as the Black Death finished its sweep of West Asia, North Africa, and Europe. I can elaborate later but in short this led to a _massive_ shift in the serf/lord power dynamic).

High Fantasy and Medieval Fantasy, meanwhile, tends to take place around the 1420s, at least technologically. This is when plate armour had become well-established in battles (see also: Agincourt in 1415), alongside extensive use of both crossbows and regular bows in combat. Certain armies still use trebuchets and ballistae, while the hot new thing is the (seemingly) humble cannon, which some people were even taking and turning into the first hand-cannons. Not super accurate, but bloody effective. 

However! A lot of medieval fantasy settings _say_ they're set in earlier periods. Particularly if it ever mentions King Arthur, Charlemagne, or Robin Hood, we're talking about a historical mismatch of (up to) 400 years! That's like making a game set in Renaissance Italy but everyone's using M16s and carpet bombing the Venetians


* This date is highly contentious. You'll even find some scholars who argue the W. Roman Empire _never_ fell, just retreated into its borders until it became a city-state again. But, y'know. One city an empire doth not make. 
(The Italians will kill me for this)

Author: @SoloGamer42
Content:
Something else about the from soft franchise( I'm talking about their entire lineage going all the way back to kingsfield and the predecessor to bloodborne Shadow Tower Abyss) is that I got in the Dark Souls because of bloodborne. Bloodborne was my first from soft game and it was incredibly difficult. I believe I died like 700 times just in the very first new game cycle before beating the game for the first time. And I remember getting frustrated with the game but never thinking the game was way too difficult. That made me want to play some of the other games and I started with the original Dark Souls then proceeded to play Demon's Souls. It wasn't until the remaster of Dark Souls 2 that I managed to play that game and sink 448 hours in a single save file. Afterwards it wasn't until 2022 that I played the original kingsfield and finally Eternal ring before completing Elden ring 100%. I know I make a lot of comments on videos I'm passionate about or topics I'm passionate about that are ridiculously long but sharing opinions and stories are what make comments so enjoyable to read aside from the humerus ones. The only game in the franchise that I have not completed and that's just because I have no interest in it is sekiro. But without bloodborne I would have never gotten the souls franchise and I would have never gotten the urge to actually get better in a single player game, and I would have never gotten to the souls like sub-genre that transpired because of those games. I've shared my opinions on Elden ring several times in several different videos about these games but if one game out of the franchise is a game that I actively don't want to replay a dozen times but genuinely respect an overall did enjoy my New Game Plus- that is a testament to how good these games are. I do prefer the older from soft from 2009 to 2019 but I cannot deny they have created a legacy that will go down in history as the premier difficult game series.

Dark Souls II may be my favorite in the entire series but I cannot deny that without experiencing the others you cannot really appreciate your favorites.

Author: @giantmonsterdad
Content:
Sean, if you see any of my comments ever, please see this one: you need to play Fire Emblem: Three Houses AND THEN Fire Emblem Warriors: Three Hopes. They're the medieval aesthetic, they have the perfect mix of good writing and good cast just like you want, and they have (imho) the perfect balance of childish humor and grimdark the world is on your shoulders. And, since you seem to be someone who likes replay-ability, they have save game plus out the ass, and multiple storylines with multiple endings (and that doesn't even touch the relationship/romance system).

The rest of these are lesser rec's that I don't think you'd get as much out of, but I'm including anyways just in case. Specifically of the Final Fantasy variety, Final Fantasy Tactics: War of the Lions. It scratches that specific itch for me that you're talking about. Granted, I did play it when I was in grade school (and, from what I see online, it is getting remastered, so you may want to wait for that), but it was phenomenal from what I remember. Another FF rec, I know you said you didn't want too mechanical, but a highly underrated FF is FFXII. It really does lean in to the class system, to the exploration, to kingdoms and intrigue and the like. Related, a Square Enix game like FFXII, Star Ocean: Till the End of Time. It's technically a sequel, but you can play it without having played any of the others (I did, and I loved it), and it is tech meets medieval, but it's, imho, incredibly unique in how it goes about it, and i would say to go in completely spoiler free, because just. Hoo boy will it get you if you do.

Lastly, if you want to go just, full medieval wacky (and I don't exactly mean like, childish wacky, just fun time slicing and dicing without a care), then there is exactly one game I would hand to you on a platter: MediEvil (2019). I grew up playing the original, the 2019 remake is worth it, don't listen to the fun police critics.

Anyways if you read all that, then good luck on finding fun games and I hope you have a great day!

Author: @Sinhesthysia
Content:
I know I'm almost certainly not the first person to tell you this, but Sean. Before you fo DS2 in one vid for this series, replay it on your own time. And don't try and use the most optimal stuff, just use something that looks fun. And most of all, take your time. DS2 is indeed very different from the rest of the series, but that's not inherently a bad thing. There are so many cool level details, voice actors, small mechanics, and overall just awesome stuff in DS2. Don't try and rush it, take your time clearing areas--even sometimes on runbacks. I can't promise you will love it, because it's ultimately a subjective experience, but I pray you go back and give it a chance with an open mind. Don't think about what the general community says about the game, find what you think about it.
Also I'm ecstatic to see you cover Demons Souls, this game holds a special place in my heart just like DS2 and Bloodborne do.

Content:
It's not exactly the same thing, but have you considered the Baldur's Gate games? I'm not just talking about the latest one that made the saga famous, but the original ones from 1998, 2001 and 2016 (Tales of the Sword Coast, Shadows of Amn and Siege of Dragon Spear)... it's a lot more d&d-ish than FF9, for obvious reasons, but it sounds to me like the elements you enjoy the most about FF9 are the high fantasy elements.
The graphics are *very* old fashioned, but gods, some of those had great writing, especially SoA.
BG3 is okay too, but you have a slightly lesser experience if you don't know the originals.

Author: @SlueBuede
Content:
I like Jack and his stuff, but he is shortsighted.

To say Lord of the Rings was better for being cut and changed while criticizing some for avoiding Berserk due to its content is most arrogant.

Most importantly, some folk just wouldn’t be able to have a good night’s sleep with that stuff floating around in their heads, or it would resurface painful memories.

Less importantly, there are also deep morals in Lord of the Rings, which, fair play, Jack is giving it a fair shake - however, to turn the wise Poet Gimli into some oaf is a great disservice to the character, or to omit the toil and strains this conflict puts the orcs (all involved really) under - I am bad at putting things into words but you know what I mean.

The way to enjoy Lord of the Rings is to forget about the movies, think of it as a whole new story, and think about it as though an old man is telling it to you. This way, you avoid the expectations of event sequence and volume in the movies (I know, because I saw the movies first and I read the book like this the first three times).

Maybe the part about Berserk was sarcasm, as I have a hard time discerning.

Also, I am only a big Tolkien fan, and I have never read One Piece or Berserk. I have only read some of JoJo’s.

Author: @UseZapCannon
Content:
For anyone in the audience still confused about World Tendency, it's like ... a light-side/dark-side type mechanic that applies to each of the individual zones. It goes closer to White World Tendency when you kill a boss (of which there are a limited number), and to Black World Tendency when you die in human form in the zone

Since each area only has 3 or 4 bosses, it's possible to go so far Black that you can't reach White anymore — which is bad, because every zone has an NPC you can only meet/items you can only reach if the zone's tendency is Pure White

So Bonk warps back to the hub area to die every time he becomes human, so that he won't die in a zone and affect its World Tendency

Author: @duchessskye4072
Content:
On the bastard sword: generally the way that the term is modernly used is indeed the way you said it which is about a sword that is sort of "in between" a one and two handed sword. The issue with that definition of course being how you define those lines, and at which point a sword becomes exclusively a two handed sword. The term 'longsword' is in use for swords that are largely meant to be used in two hands however most of these are still useable one-handed and manuals with these swords do have single-handed techniques with them which would make that category of sword fit into the moden usage of 'bastard sword' as well.

Historically the word bastard sword is found but it means something completely different. What it means is unknown since it's a pretty ambiguous term. Some have suggested it might mean swords which don't have maker's marks on them, therefore being 'bastards' since they aren't marked. Or maybe it's something else, there's really no solid explanation.

Author: @RainMakeR_Workshop
Content: Not quite right on Bastard Swords. All Bastard Swords are Longswords, but not all Longswords are Bastard Swords. And its not quite as simple as grip length that makes something a Bastard Sword. Its more that it can be used two handed or one handed without being so long that its unwieldly in one hand. That CAN be a grip that you can 't quite fit two hands on, making a "Hand and a Half Sword", which is used interchangeably with Bastard Sword. But it can also be a grip with plenty of room for two hands and a shorter blade.

Content:
Have you tried much Dark and Darker? It's a medieval style dungeon game , with 1 to 3 player teams so you could team up with Evelyn or friends, the fighting is gritty and crunchy, the designs are immersive and very dungeons ans dragons. Classes make sense warriors with big weapons,bards with quick rapier strikes and songs that buff allies or debuff enemies, theives that sneak in the shadows and assassinate people and run away like cowards. 

 There's a level up system and skills to tailer your builds slightly, and the pvevp style keeps you tense that you could lose it all at any moment while stealing loot and equipment.

The game came out a while ago and has been getting regular updates with more quests to chase down new areas and bosses and new characters like druids and warlocks. Maybe a few games would scratch that itch?

Author: @barunmajumdar679
Content:
I wish there was a third ending in Demon's Souls. In the first ending, you clean up the mess and then fix it. In the second ending, you become the one making the mess. I would love a possible third ending where you stay behind within the Old One as a guardian. If someone somehow were to rediscover the soul arts, you would be there to put an end to it before they go too far. 

After playing Demon's Souls myself (I am not an original Demon's Souls player) and then playing the original, I noticed that it feels different compared to the remake. It's not just the graphics; the art direction has a certain atmosphere and vibe that the remake somewhat diminishes for me. While the remake is still a good game and looks fantastic—combining realistic aspects with the game's basic aesthetic—it does lose some of the original's charm. If they were to make a Bloodborne or Dark Souls remake, it’s essential that they capture the original vibe to finish the work properly. Regarding the Demon's Souls remake, I wish they had added more content to the new version. I’m sure the creators had ideas they couldn't implement in the original for various reasons, and they could have done so here. This would allow new players to experience all-new content while also providing something for old players to discover.

Content: I know you'll love ds2 a lot more than you expect, theres aspects of the game that are so overlooked and deserve love and attention. The dlc content, the uniqie game mechanics, puzzles and level design. Not to mention the awesome ng+ content that is unique to ds2 only. Highly recommend looking at and exploring things you could miss in ds2. Main advice, never rush an area, there are intended ways to tackle every encounter. I have hundreds of hours in that game and i can say theres so many fun ways to navigate the game and content that appears only after returning to certain areas, not to mention hidden areas being very plentiful. And the dlc content is by far my favorite in the series right next to Bloodbornes old hunters and artorias of the abyss. Also you can respecc stats back at the old ladies at the start by using soul vessels, and you can use bonfire aesetics to send a single area into its ng+ version and refight bosses, have new upgraded item locations, and new enemies placed in. I hope you see this.

Author: @Casioli-Ravioli
Content:
I never had the desire to play any of the FromSoft games because Im not a fan of games that are intentionally hard, so for years I was just like "eh, it's not really my thing" but I knew other people loved it.

I now rewatch his Dark Souls and Dark Souls 3 videos almost weekly to have on in the background while Im doing stuff. It helps so much, and I love listening to him talk about stuff when he goes off on his little side note tangents. And his love for these games has been so infectious that despite never knowing anything much about any of these games, Im now looking up lore and trying to understand the story and even plan to buy Dark Souls at some point in the near future. His love for these games made me start to want to play and love the games I swore would never be for me. So, thank you, Seán (and huge thanks to your editors, too)!

Edit: Thank you guys so much for tips and encouragement, I appreciate your suggestions! I'll have to look into it and see if Elden Ring might be better to start off with (I'll still play Dark Souls 1 & 3 at some point).

Content: Not sure if this will be read or not but to get access to the items in the outer dragon area of 1-1 (Boletaria's first area), you need to kill the Red Dragon in 1-2 (the bridge). You can do it by shooting the dragon with a bow when it flies past while you're at the top of the tower-like parts. It will take a long time of you just standing still, shooting arrows as the dragon has a lot of health. The blue dragon can be killed in 1-4, but you can get all of the meaningful items without killing them. For instance, Demon's Souls' iteration of Havel's Ring (Ring of Great Strength) is found there.

Author: @iz2933
Content:
These recommendations wont exactly fit what youre looking for (as i think the games you love just set the bar really high and are the greatest of their kind, honestly) but might at least get you something similar to try.

Triangle Strategy and Unicorn Overlord, match the aesthetic but are tactical RPGs. Ive not heard phenomenal things about either but theyre fairly well received.

Octopath Traveler, youve likely heard of, matches in aesthetic and classic RPG. They also look great with their 3D pixel art.

Bravely Default doesnt hit the aesthetic much but another enjoyable RPG directly inspired by FF.

Funnily, Dragon Quest IX may be a better fit to the medieval than VIII. I played it growing up and it was great, no other experience with DQ but in hindsight the story feels like an FF.

Darkest Dungeon youve probably heard of. Roguelike but hits the aesthetic points.

I'll mention lastly Fear and Hunger. It hits the aesthetic well and is much grittier RPG. But it has some serious content warnings and definitely not YouTube friendly. Considered a very difficult game bc of the intricacies of progression and how punishing combat is. So it may not be your thing at all but the art is great on its own.

Not games but I did want to give a mention to the manga Claymore that may be really up your alley for the medieval aesthetic and the art reminding me in places of Berserk. Side mention to Dungeon Meshi for being a great medieval fantasy portrayal, though it of course revolves around food. The illustrations are great both in attention to monsters and the environments of the dungeon. Side side mention to Witch Hat Atelier for a medieval setting but its very magic/wizard focused as the title suggests. Beautiful illustrations as well.

Really enjoyed the video and the podcast moments, here's hoping the FF9 remaster/remake happens 🙏

Content:
Also, since Sean asked at 8:45, the “Medieval Times” or Middle ages in Western Europe were from around 500 to 1500 CE. West Rome fell in 476 which to some “starts” the period, and the Renaissance “starts” in Italy in 1450 (but later in other European nations). So, in general, the Middle Ages are 500-1500, with the Early Middle Ages being 500-1000, the High Middle Ages being 1000-1200, and the Late Middle Ages being 1200-1500. Early was very chaotic (the collapse of West Rome is ti thank), High had some stabilization of nations, urban areas, and religious institutions, and Late had the Black Plague, conflicts with religious institutions, and other wars and destabilized what had restabilized. The fall of the Byzantium Empire in 1453 loosed all the Classical Greek and Roman texts they had (they were the Greek speaking other half of the Roman empire after Emperor Constantine converted the whole Roman Empire to Christianity in 325 and split it in half in 330, with West Rome in Rome and East Rome in Constantinople) to Western Europe, starting with Italy (which is why the Renaissance (Rebirth of Classical thought) started there). 
… anyway, hope that cleared things up. Source… history degree that I am very close to being a certified doctoral expert in 😅. Thanks for coming to my Ted Talk. 
And yes I’m glossing over some things and ball parking some dates. This is a Youtube comment I’m writing while sprawled on my couch, not a peer reviewed essay. Please don’t be mad if I didn’t mention your particular local history 😅.

Author: @moshicko4191
Content:
12:50 the thing is it's not just nostalgia, there's an acual case to be made about original artistic intent and motivations behind remakes or supposed "upgrades"

Everyone knows on a general level that "bigger isnt always better" etc, and that having what you need to achieve your goal well is better than just always trying to have more. But not a lot of people seem to apply that idea to video games as a medium

I personally believe that realism in game graphics is more often a style decision made by execs who concern themselves with cramming as many 'features' into a game for the sake of marketability rather than an artistic choice made by someone with creative vision.

I think original games almost always look better than remakes because the original looks the way it does due to artistic decisions made by the art director, whereas a remake usually looks the way it does because someone thinks they can capitalize on the success of something great by supposedly making it "better" without understanding what made it great in the first place.

Demon's souls is by no means the worst example of this or even a particularly bad one, its just a trend I feel is prevelant and underdiscussed/understood

Author: @barunmajumdar679
Content:
I wish there was a third ending in Demon's Souls. In the first ending, you clean up the mess and then fix it. In the second ending, you become the one making the mess. I would love a possible third ending where you stay behind within the Old One as a guardian. If someone somehow were to rediscover the soul arts, you would be there to put an end to it before they go too far. 

After playing Demon's Souls myself (I am not an original Demon's Souls player) and then playing the original, I noticed that it feels different compared to the remake. It's not just the graphics; the art direction has a certain atmosphere and vibe that the remake somewhat diminishes for me. While the remake is still a good game and looks fantastic—combining realistic aspects with the game's basic aesthetic—it does lose some of the original's charm. If they were to make a Bloodborne or Dark Souls remake, it’s essential that they capture the original vibe to finish the work properly. Regarding the Demon's Souls remake, I wish they had added more content to the new version. I’m sure the creators had ideas they couldn't implement in the original for various reasons, and they could have done so here. This would allow new players to experience all-new content while also providing something for old players to discover.
